body: ## What Acting as a user and driving the app in a real browser (Playwright), I found that visiting the public **`/catalog`** page throws a React **"Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client"** error in the console on every load. ## Why it happens The CourseTable catalog queries run **only in the browser** (`enabled: isBrowser`), so during SSR they are disabled and render nothing. React Query v5 returns an *optimistic* fetching state on the first client render, so: - **Server** rendered `null` for the catalog-count badge / empty-state. - **Client's first render** painted the `Loading catalog…` badge (optimistic `isLoading === true`). Those differ, so React reports a hydration mismatch and regenerates the subtree. ## Fix Added a small `useHydrated()` hook (returns `false` on the server and on the first client render, `true` after mount) and gated the client-only query UI on `/catalog` behind it: - catalog count badge - "Loading … catalog" text - "No courses match your search" empty state This keeps the first client render identical to the server output, then reveals live query state after hydration. ## Verification - Reproduced the console error with Playwright before the change; **0 console errors** after. - Catalog search still works (e.g. searching `CPSC` returns results). - `bun run build` passes; the two changed files are ESLint/Prettier clean (remaining Prettier warnings in `catalog.tsx` are pre-existing on `main` and untouched). Note: authenticated pages could not be exercised end-to-end because the remote Supabase requires email-confirmed sign-in, which isn't available in this environment. Linear Issue: [NET-15](https://linear.app/netta-dobzinski/issue/NET-15/act-as-user)

author: chelstein
body:
Three things that finish the census as a real product — credibility, programming intel, and trends. All from data already in hand.

## 1 · Integrity monitor — keep the count credible

`_integrity_scan` scores four signals per station: **identical durations, mass simultaneous starts, one identity fanned into many sessions, an eerily flat 24h curve.** Conservative — `watch` on one strong signal, `quarantined` only on multiple, so a real station is never falsely killed (bot with identical durations → watch; real audience → clean). `GET /rdns/ratings/integrity` is the open anti-fraud monitor; `_quarantined_fids` flags gamed stations right in `/rdns/ratings/data`. Completes the trust model: crude inflation capped, verified/provisional separated, and now the *shape* of the traffic watched — openly.

## 2 · Now-playing correlation — the intel no small station ever had

`_song_audience` (`GET /rdns/station/songs`) crosses `station_playlog` (what aired + its on-air window) against `listen_sessions` (who was on): per song, **average listeners while it played, how many tuned in during it (draw) vs. left (shed), and net draw.** Ranks holders and drawers. Verified: a song that gains a listener scores +1, one that sheds −1. Real programming truth from ears, not a call-out survey.

## 3 · Trend snapshots — growth over time, not just a rolling window

The daily cron now writes a per-station census snapshot (`_snapshot_census` → `census_snapshots`, idempotent per day); `GET /rdns/station/trend` serves the trend line so the audience report shows real movement over time.

The census is now real, fast, useful (rate-card report), credibly hard to game, and it tells a station *which songs work* and *how it's growing*. A complete measurement product — with KAZM as listener zero.

Implements PRO-29 (F1) — first Phase 0 foundation step for the 8-tool support effort.

## Problem
`ARTIFACT_FILES` in `artifacts.py` hand-maintained each tool's `remove` set as the union of every other tool's `create` paths. O(n²): adding a tool meant editing every other tool's entry, and the sets could silently drift.

`_TOOL_CREATE` (create sets) is now the single source of truth. `_build_artifact_files()` derives each `remove` set as **(union of every other tool's creates) ∪ legacy artifacts** (`.kilocode/`, `custom_instructions/`, `rules/`). Adding a tool = one `_TOOL_CREATE` entry; existing tools automatically learn to clean it up.

The derived `ARTIFACT_FILES` is **exactly equal** to the previous hand-written map for all 6 tools (verified). Public shape unchanged, so `ArtifactManager` and all consumers are untouched.

body:
## P0 safety gap: prod capture discarded the crisis result

Found by the persona-validate capture panel — the **Safety expert scored this surface 0/2**, and **six of eleven personas independently flagged the same defect** (E1/E2/E3/E4, U01/U02).

The prod deep-space `CaptureView` (the primary 담기 intake, all 5 modes) saved every capture via `createRecord({kind:"note", withFollowup:false})` but **discarded the return value**. On that path `createRecord` runs the local crisis lexicon and returns `{followup:{zone:"red"}}` when the text trips crisis detection — *precisely so the screen can fire its crisis modal* (create.ts comment). `CaptureView` only called `setSaved(true)`, so **a user typing self-harm content into the primary capture got a cheerful "저장됨" and no hotline** — while every other save path (journal, memo, OCR, voice) surfaces one.

### Fix
`savePiece` now reads the result and, on a red zone, opens `CrisisRouter` with the **same locale/minor-aware hotline the journal path uses** (`KR_1388` minor · `KR_109` KR adult · `GLOBAL_988` otherwise). This is a pure replication of the proven `capture.tsx` `handleJournalSubmit` pattern using the existing `CrisisRouter` + classifier — **no new crisis logic**.

### Scope / flagged for maintainer
- Fixes crisis **routing** for the ko/en (supported) crisis locales.
- **Not** addressed (separate clinical-content item, flagged to Simon): the E5 finding that `locale` collapses to `en` for es/pt/id, and the crisis lexicon has no per-language terms — a Spanish/Portuguese/Indonesian crisis capture isn't classified at all. That needs reviewed per-language crisis lexicons, which shouldn't be authored autonomously.

### Verify
`npm run verify` green — 330 suites / 2472 tests, exit 0. On-device e2e (type a crisis phrase → hotline modal) to follow post-merge.

author: seanshairah
body:
## Summary

Fixes the **"Paynow declined the request."** error seen on both EcoCash Express and the web-redirect payment in production.

**Root cause:** Paynow returns its API response as a URL-encoded, `&`-separated query string (`status=Ok&browserurl=...&pollurl=...&hash=...`), but `parsePaynowResponse` split on **newlines** only. It therefore read the entire response as a single `status` value like `"Ok&browserurl=…"`, which never equals `"ok"` — so even a **successful** initiate/poll was treated as declined. This affected every live `initiatetransaction` (web) and `remotetransaction` (EcoCash Express) call, plus status polling.

**Fix:**
- Parse Paynow responses as a proper URL query string (split on `&` and newlines, handle `+`/percent-encoding).
- Surface Paynow's real `status`/`error` message instead of the generic fallback, so any genuine decline (e.g. Express not enabled on the integration) is now visible.

The result webhook already parsed correctly (`URLSearchParams`) and is unchanged.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` passes.

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
## Summary

This PR fixes a payload size bug in auto-mode memory recall responses that was causing silent recall failures across the plugin ecosystem.

### Root Cause

`toMemoryRecallResponse()` in `src/lib/memory/api/recall.ts` was unconditionally serializing `conflicts[]` and `conflictStats` into every recall response. Each conflict pair contains the full article content of both sides, and on broad queries (e.g. multi-turn auto-recall) this field could account for **>98% of the response body** — pushing payloads past the plugin's 1 MB `MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES` limit and producing `response body is too large` errors that dropped memory context entirely.

### Fix

Conditionally omit `conflicts` and `conflictStats` when `response.mode === "auto"`. The plugin's auto-mode handler only consumes `promptInjectionText`, so these fields are dead weight in that path. Inspection mode (used by the `noosphere_recall` tool) continues to receive full conflict data unchanged.

### Impact

| Query (auto, 10 results) | Before | After | Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `the project status update` | 1,343,629 bytes | ~15,561 bytes | **98.8%** |
| `noosphere memory` | 338,432 bytes | ~15 KB | 95% |
| `serianis deployment` | 60,626 bytes | ~15 KB | 75% |

### Plugin compatibility

No plugin-side changes required. All consumer plugins (OpenClaw, Hermes, Opencode, Kilo Code) already treat `conflicts` as optional in `NoosphereRecallResponse` and handle the undefined case correctly.

### Tests

Two new regression tests in `src/__tests__/memory/api-recall.test.ts`:
- **Auto mode** asserts `conflicts` and `conflictStats` are omitted
- **Inspection mode** asserts both fields are still present

This guards against future regressions if someone re-introduces unconditional conflict serialization.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: hiro-o918
body:
## Summary

Adds the release infrastructure needed to publish `rinkaku`: MIT license, a
`rinkaku-core` (lib) / `rinkaku` (bin) crate split so `cargo install rinkaku`
resolves correctly, crates.io metadata, release-please for automated
CHANGELOG/version PRs, a tag-triggered build-and-publish pipeline
(cross-compiled binaries + crates.io + Homebrew tap), an install script, and
updated README installation docs. Conventions are carried over from
`hiro-o918/skem` (release-please + build-and-publish shape, install.sh) and
`hiro-o918/awsctx` (Homebrew tap bump job).

This PR intentionally stays in **draft**: the workflows cannot be exercised
end-to-end until the secrets listed below are configured, and the Homebrew
tap needs a one-time manual bootstrap (see "Required secrets setup" and
"First release checklist").

## What changed, per area

1. **LICENSE** — MIT, copyright holder confirmed via `git log`
   (Hironori Yamamoto), same template as skem's LICENSE.
2. **Crate split** — `rinkaku-core` becomes lib-only (no `[[bin]]`); new
   `rinkaku` crate holds `main.rs` plus CLI-only deps (`clap`, `log`,
   `env_logger`), depending on `rinkaku-core` via `path` + `version`.
   `cargo install rinkaku` requires a crate literally named `rinkaku` with a
   `[[bin]]` — a bin embedded in `rinkaku-core` cannot satisfy that. Recorded
   as an amendment to ADR-0001 (this was already the intended end-state per
   the original ADR text, just deferred in the bootstrap PR).
3. **Cargo metadata** — `description` / `license` / `repository` / `readme`
   / `keywords` (`diff`, `tree-sitter`, `code-review`, `llm`) / `categories`
   on both crates. `version` stays `0.1.0`.
4. **release-please** (`.github/workflows/release-main.yaml` +
   `.github/release-please/`) — same GitHub App token pattern as skem
   (`THIS_GITHUB_APP_ID` / `THIS_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`). Config differs
   from skem (single crate) because rinkaku is a two-crate workspace: uses
   the `cargo-workspace` plugin (`merge: false`) to bump both `Cargo.toml`
   files + the lockfile, plus `linked-versions` to keep `rinkaku-core` and
   `rinkaku` on the same version (matching `workspace.package.version`
   inherited by both crates).
5. **build-and-publish** (`.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yaml`) — same
   shape as skem: linux/macos × x86_64/aarch64 cross-build → tar.gz →
   `gh release upload`, gated by the shared `wc-rust-test.yaml`. Adds a
   `publish-crates` job (rinkaku-core first, then rinkaku, with a 30s wait
   for crates.io indexing in between — rinkaku depends on rinkaku-core by
   registry version, not path, once published) and a `publish-homebrew` job.
6. **Homebrew tap** (`publish-homebrew` job) — `mislav/bump-homebrew-formula-action`,
   same as awsctx's `homebrew-release.yml`, updating
   `Formula/rinkaku.rb` in `hiro-o918/homebrew-tap` from the
   `x86_64-apple-darwin` tarball after each release.
7. **install.sh** — adapted from skem's (same target-triple naming as this
   repo's release tarballs). Passes `shellcheck` with no warnings.
8. **README** — Installation section now documents all four methods
   (Homebrew, install script, `cargo install`, manual GitHub Releases
   download) plus a Development note on the two-crate layout.

## cargo publish --dry-run results

- `cargo publish -p rinkaku-core --dry-run --allow-dirty` — **passes**
  (packages, verifies, and would upload 16 files / ~50KiB compressed).
- `cargo publish -p rinkaku --dry-run --allow-dirty` — **fails** with
  `no matching package named rinkaku-core found (location searched:
  crates.io index)`. This is expected per the task: `rinkaku` depends on
  `rinkaku-core` by registry version, and `rinkaku-core` isn't published
  yet, so a solo dry-run for `rinkaku` can't resolve it. The
  `publish-crates` job publishes `rinkaku-core` first for this reason; a
  real `cargo publish -p rinkaku` will resolve correctly once
  `rinkaku-core` exists on crates.io.

## Required secrets setup

`gh secret list --repo hiro-o918/rinkaku` currently returns **no secrets at
all**. The following must be configured before the release workflows can
run:

| Secret | Used by | How to obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `THIS_GITHUB_APP_ID` | `release-main.yaml`, `wc-rust-test.yaml`, `build-and-publish.yaml` (`publish-homebrew`) | Same GitHub App already used by skem (`gh secret list --repo hiro-o918/skem` shows it configured there). If it's the same App, copy its App ID; otherwise create a GitHub App with `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write` permissions and install it on `hiro-o918/rinkaku`. |
| `THIS_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | same as above | Private key (PEM) generated for that GitHub App. |
| `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` | `build-and-publish.yaml` (`publish-crates`) | Generate at https://crates.io/settings/tokens with publish scope for `rinkaku-core` and `rinkaku` (or an unscoped token for a personal account). |

`publish-homebrew` uses `actions/create-github-app-token` to mint a
short-lived installation token scoped to `hiro-o918/homebrew-tap`, instead of
a long-lived PAT. This requires the GitHub App backing
`THIS_GITHUB_APP_ID` / `THIS_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` to additionally satisfy:

- **Contents: Read and write** permission (needed to push the formula bump
  commit).
- Be **installed on `hiro-o918/homebrew-tap`** as well as
  `hiro-o918/rinkaku` — the `repositories: homebrew-tap` input in the
  `create-github-app-token` step scopes the minted token to that repo, but
  the token generation itself fails if the App isn't installed there.

Additionally, **`Formula/rinkaku.rb` does not yet exist in
`hiro-o918/homebrew-tap`**. `mislav/bump-homebrew-formula-action` updates
fields in an existing formula file, it does not create one. A one-time
manual commit to `hiro-o918/homebrew-tap` is needed before the first
`publish-homebrew` run, e.g.:

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

class Rinkaku < Formula
    desc "Condense PR diffs into signatures and their dependencies for LLM-friendly review"
    homepage "https://github.com/hiro-o918/rinkaku"
    version "0.1.0"
    license "MIT"
    url "https://github.com/hiro-o918/rinkaku/releases/download/v0.1.0/rinkaku-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
    sha256 "<filled in after the first release>"

    def install
        bin.install "rinkaku"
    end

    test do
        system "#{bin}/rinkaku", "--version"
    end
end
```

## First release checklist (after this PR is merged)

1. Configure the four secrets above on `hiro-o918/rinkaku`.
2. Create the initial `Formula/rinkaku.rb` in `hiro-o918/homebrew-tap` (see
   snippet above; the sha256 can be a placeholder — the first
   `publish-homebrew` run overwrites it).
3. Merge this PR's changes into `main` (already required to get here).
4. release-please opens its first release PR automatically on the next
   push to `main` after secrets are set — review and merge it.
5. Merging the release-please PR tags `main` (e.g. `v0.1.0`), which
   triggers `build-and-publish.yaml`: cross-compiled binaries uploaded to
   the GitHub Release, `rinkaku-core` then `rinkaku` published to
   crates.io, and `Formula/rinkaku.rb` bumped in the tap.
6. Verify: `cargo install rinkaku`, `brew install hiro-o918/tap/rinkaku`,
   and the install script all succeed against the new release.
7. Once verified, un-draft (or close and re-open as ready) — this PR is
   intentionally left in draft per the task since none of the workflow
   behavior can be exercised until step 1 is done.

## Differences from the reference repos (skem / awsctx / drydock)

- **skem** has no `cargo publish` step at all (never published to
  crates.io) and no Homebrew tap integration — both are new here, not
  copied.
- **skem** is a single crate; the release-please config here additionally
  uses the `cargo-workspace` + `linked-versions` plugins to keep two
  crates in lockstep, which skem's config doesn't need.
- **awsctx**'s `release.yml` / `lint.yml` are an older, pre-GitHub-App-token
  generation of this repo's auto

## Summary

Supabase Security Advisor flagged `rls_disabled_in_public` on project **DataForgedb** (`embvfponjxejbtrkryzs`).

- On 2026-06-02, `sql/supabase_rls_and_indexes.sql` was run by hand in the Supabase SQL editor, enabling RLS on every public table that existed at that time. That script is **not** wired into the deploy pipeline.
- Ten tables created by later migrations (`20260606_01` .. `20260623_01`) never got the same treatment and shipped with RLS disabled: `agent_memories`, `context_packs`, `model_outcomes`, `cssa_decisions`, `cssa_authorizations`, `cssa_outcomes`, `cssa_counters`, `cssa_quota_reservations`, `cssa_authorization_consumptions`, `supabase_log_events`.
- This ecosystem has no Supabase end-user auth or multitenancy — every legitimate access path uses the Postgres **owner role**, which bypasses RLS regardless of policies. RLS-enabled-with-zero-policies only denies Supabase's PostgREST anon/authenticated Data API, which nothing here is meant to use for these tables. This matches the existing precedent for `llm_secrets`/`api_keys` (self-protect at creation) and the original hardening script — so a deny-all posture, no new policies, is both correct and the smallest fix.

## What changed

- **New:** `alembic/versions/20260711_01_enable_rls_on_drifted_public_tables.py` — runs the same idempotent RLS-enable scan via `alembic upgrade head`, which already runs automatically on every deploy (`scripts/render-build.sh`). Unlike the manual SQL-editor script, this self-heals the drift class going forward instead of relying on someone remembering to re-run a script. Downgrade is a deliberate no-op — a rollback can never reopen these tables.
- **New:** `tests/test_security/test_rls_public_tables.py` — real-Postgres integration test (RLS can't be exercised on the sqlite test DB), opt-in via `DATAFORGE_RLS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`. Asserts RLS is enabled on all 10 tables and that the owner role can still read/write them.
- **Docs only:** `sql/supabase_rls_and_indexes.sql` — added a drift-warning note pointing at the new migration.

## Test plan

Verified locally against a throwaway Postgres 16 + pgvector instance (sandbox had no live DB/CLI access otherwise):

- [x] `alembic heads`/`alembic history` — chain resolves to a single head, no branching
- [x] `alembic upgrade ... --sql` (offline) — confirmed exact SQL emitted; `alembic downgrade ... --sql` confirmed rollback only rewinds version bookkeeping, no RLS disabled
- [x] Migration applied for real against a throwaway Postgres DB seeded with the 10 tables' real schemas: all 10 + `alembic_version` show `relrowsecurity = true`; a pre-existing RLS'd table used as a negative control was untouched
- [x] Owner role: insert/select on `cssa_counters` succeeded (bypass intact)
- [x] Non-owner role with explicit `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`UPDATE` grants (simulating Supabase `anon`/`authenticated`) denied on all three operations despite the grants
- [ ] Not yet applied to the production Supabase database — no production credentials available in this session
- [ ] Supabase Advisor not yet rechecked post-deploy

**Note (out of scope, discovered during verification):** migration `20260401_01_runtime_promotion_execution_handoff.py` defines an index identifier that exceeds Postgres's 63-character limit, which blocks a true from-scratch `alembic upgrade head` on a brand-new database. Unrelated to this fix — flagging for separate triage.

## Relevant issues

Fixes #32951

## Linear ticket

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

`stream_chunk_builder` (`litellm/main.py`) assumed every element of `chunks` supports string-key indexing (`c["choices"]`). On the streaming `/v1/messages` (`call_type=anthropic_messages`) route the logging/usage assembly path can hand it raw SSE `bytes`, so `c["choices"]` raised `TypeError: byte indices must be integers or slices, not str`, which the function re-wrapped as a generic `APIError(500, "Error building chunks for logging/streaming usage calculation")` at the tail of an otherwise successful, already-billed stream

The fix drops raw byte/str payloads before the chunks reach `ChunkProcessor`, so a leaked `bytes` chunk can no longer crash the assembly. The reporter notes that the exact code path that appends a `bytes` element on this route is not pinned, so the guard sits at the verified crash site where every caller of `stream_chunk_builder` funnels through

```python
if not chunks:
    return None

chunks = [chunk for chunk in chunks if not isinstance(chunk, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview, str))]
if not chunks:

```

author: bug-ops
body:
## Summary

`PluginManager::add_remote` and `download_archive` in `crates/zeph-plugins/src/manager/registry.rs` called `response.bytes()` unconditionally with no upper bound on body size, unlike `download_and_extract`, which already rejected an oversized `Content-Length` before reading the body. This allowed a malicious or compromised host to exhaust process memory (CWE-400):

- `add_remote` — manual permanent plugin install path.
- `download_archive` — backs the unattended `check_auto_updates`/`update_one_plugin` path, which runs on every process startup for any plugin with `auto_update = true`.

This closes the residual gap left by #6104, which consolidated the anti-downgrade HTTPS client across all three call sites but did not also consolidate the size check.

## Changes

- Added a shared `fetch_archive_bytes` helper (`crates/zeph-plugins/src/manager/registry.rs`) that bundles `get_https_safe` with a `Content-Length` pre-check against `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` (52 MiB), rejecting oversized responses before the body is read.
- `add_remote`, `download_archive`, and `download_and_extract` all now call this single helper — there is exactly one place enforcing the cap instead of one (previously only `download_and_extract`).
- Added two regression tests exercising the cap via a real oversized response body (`add_remote_rejects_oversized_content_length`, `check_auto_updates_rejects_oversized_content_length`).

## Scope note

Matching `download_and_extract`'s existing behavior, the cap is `Content-Length`-based and enforced before the body read, not during a streamed read. A host that omits or lies about `Content-Length` (e.g. via chunked transfer-encoding) is not caught by this check — this is a pre-existing gap shared with `download_and_extract`'s original implementation, not a new one introduced here, and is out of scope for this issue. Documented as a known gap in `CHANGELOG.md` and `.local/testing/playbooks/plugins.md`; a streaming-enforced follow-up may be worth filing separately.

Each active, non-trial, recurring subscription normalizes to a daily rate (`cost / cycle_days`: Weekly=7, Monthly=30, Yearly=365), summed, then projected `*7`/`*30`/`*365`. `OneTime` subscriptions purchased in the current calendar year sum separately into `OneTimeThisYear`. author: milosde111
body:
## What

`adaptive_hybrid_attention(..., causal=True)` leaked the future through its global
branch. Every other hybrid variant threads `causal` into both branches, but the
adaptive one called `adaptive_spectral_global_mix(q, v, ...)` with no `causal`
argument — and the function had no such parameter.

Its global branch was unconditionally non-causal:
- a zero-phase rfft low-pass that mixes V across the whole sequence, and
- a gate derived from `q.mean(dim=-2)` — a mean over *every* query, including future ones.

So with `--causal`, `out[t]` depended on `v[t+1:]` and `q[t+1:]` (weight = `global_weight`,
default 0.15). This is the exact defect deferred as a follow-up in the
`spectral_global_mix` causality fix (commit d1ed5ce): *"adaptive_spectral_global_mix
has a separate causal defect (its gate averages over future queries) and is left for
a follow-up."*

## Fix

- Add a `causal` parameter to `adaptive_spectral_global_mix` and route it from
  `adaptive_hybrid_attention`.
- The causal branch replaces both leaks with strictly-past-only counterparts:
  - **V:** the EMA linear (zero-padded) convolution with partial-mass renormalization —
    the same recipe already used by `spectral_global_mix`'s causal branch.
  - **Gate:** a running (cumulative) mean of Q up to position `t` instead of the
    whole-sequence mean, converging to the non-causal mean at the last position.
- The non-causal path is unchanged.

## Tests

New `tests/test_adaptive_spectral_causal.py`:
- future-perturbation no-leak, at both the mixer and end-to-end `adaptive_hybrid_attention` level;
- `freq_decay=0` reduces to a running-gated V (identity low-pass);
- non-causal path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Confirmed the leak test fails on the pre-fix code (~8e-3 leakage) and passes after.
All existing attention tests (31/31) still pass.

body:
Follow-up to #2385. `choose-gui` was the first symptom of this
failure class in the m4mac closure; `kitty` is the next.

## Symptom

The m4mac CI build now advances past choose-gui but hits the same
`Trace/BPT trap: 5` in the cctools `ld` wrapper at the
`glfw-cocoa.so` link step:

```
clang ... -framework Cocoa -framework IOKit ... -o build/kitty/glfw-cocoa.so
/nix/store/...cctools-.../bin/ld: line 292: 24087 Trace/BPT trap: 5
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 133
```

Failing run: https://github.com/prismatic-koi/nixos-config/actions/runs/29171272201

## Fix

Same shape as the choose-gui override in #2385 — force the link step
through `lld`:

```nix
nativeBuildInputs = (old.nativeBuildInputs or [ ]) ++ [ final.llvmPackages.lld ];
env = (old.env or { }) // {
  NIX_CFLAGS_LINK = ((old.env.NIX_CFLAGS_LINK or "") + " -fuse-ld=lld");
};
```

## Pattern origin

Unlike choose-gui (where we mirrored the maintainer shape used for
`python3Packages.pyobjc-framework-Cocoa`), this is a direct mirror of
the actual upstream fix for this exact package:

- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/539908 ("kitty: work around
  ld64 hardening issue") — merged to `master` on 2026-07-09 as
  commit `d2a7c286bdb34760a36d51b5deb37b5e736e5c60`.

Our flake follows `nixos-unstable`, and that channel has **not yet**
advanced past `d2a7c286` — the bump we picked up in #2380 stopped at
`0bb7ec5`, which predates the kitty fix (confirmed via
`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). So we mirror the upstream override
locally until the channel catches up.

## Removal condition

The block-comment in `overlays/default.nix` documents both paths.
Delete this override once **either**:

1. our `nixos-unstable` flake-follow advances past nixpkgs commit
   `d2a7c286bdb34760a36d51b5deb37b5e736e5c60` — at which point
   upstream carries the same override and ours is a duplicate; **or**
2. https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/536365 ("ld64: disable
   hardening again") lands and the whole workaround train unwinds —
   at which point the underlying regression is gone and every
   per-package fix in this class (including upstream's own) becomes
   dead weight.

Whichever comes first.

## Validation

- `nixfmt .` clean.
- `nix-instantiate --eval --expr 'builtins.getFlake (toString ./.)'` — OK.
- Cross-checked the applied override on the m4mac config from this
  Linux worktree (same shape as the #2385 spot check):
  ```
  m4mac.pkgs.kitty.drvAttrs.NIX_CFLAGS_LINK  -> " -fuse-ld=lld"
  builtins.length nativeBuildInputs           -> 27 (was 26; lld added)
  m4mac.pkgs.choose-gui unchanged (regression) -> still 27 / " -fuse-ld=lld"
  ```
- Real build validation is post-merge (build-and-cache runs on push
  to `main`, not on PRs).

## Note on future iterations

There's a real chance more packages in the m4mac closure will surface
the same failure class as the build gets further. Not preemptively
adding overlays for packages we can't confirm are in the closure —
we'll let the next build tell us.

## H5 — the Cooper fix (PIPELINE_HARDENING_PLAN.md §3)

Ownership becomes **persisted section-level source data inherited by chunks**, replacing the per-chunk lexical guess over isolated 800-char fragments (F3 second half, F12). A Result paragraph with zero entity tokens under a `# Cooper.ai — Data Engineering` heading now inherits the section's entity — it can never again be silently assigned to a lexically-similar wrong entity or left to chance.

### What changed

- **Chunking consumes elements, not flat text** — `chunk_elements` (`domain/chunking.py`): one chunk per H4 source element; oversized elements split at sentence boundaries; **never across an element boundary**. Span refs move to raw-text coordinates (the immutable H2 payload), so chunk identity survives normalizer changes.
- **Migration `0019`**: `evidence` gains `element_id` (indexed), `sequence_index`, `section_path` — document order and the governing heading trail are columns, not parses of `source_ref`. `list_assigned_evidence` orders by them (legacy rows keep insertion order behind).
- **Two-stage assignment**: one ownership decision per top-level section subtree (`SectionAssigner` — heuristic scores heading tokens before body vocabulary, refuses ties at both stages; `LlmSectionAssigner` sees the heading trail + bounded body summary, prompt truncations counted in the report + logged), then chunks inherit as `assignment_method='section'`. READMEs stay repo-owned — now correct by construction. Structureless sources keep the per-chunk assigner, still refusing ties.
- **Human corrections at decision level**: `POST /roster/sections/{element_id}/assign` pins a whole subtree `human`; H1's pin protects it (and single-chunk pins) against machine re-runs. The unassigned queue gains `element_id` + `section_path`.
- **Rollback lever**: `STRUCTURED_ASSIGNMENT=false` restores the flat-text path verbatim (kept for one release); the schema stays either way.

### Acceptance (plan §H5)

- ✅ A chunk under a heading naming entity X can never be silently assigned to entity Y — Cooper regression fixture in `tests/test_section_ownership.py`
- ✅ Problem and Result within one section cannot receive different owners
- ✅ Document order reconstructable from columns for every post-H5 row

### Known gap, by design

Re-runs leave pre-H5 normalized-space rows in place alongside the new element-derived chunks — supersession (`evidence.is_active`) is **H6**, which needs exactly this element identity to supersede precisely. Recommend a live u1 corpus re-run comparison against the current human-corrected assignments before relying on the new default (the plan's gate).

### Verification

`ruff check` + `ruff format` clean, `mypy app` clean, **874 passed** offline with zero credentials (39 new tests: Cooper regression, boundary-split uniform ownership, heading-beats-vocabulary, tie refusals, order round-trip, section pin + H1 survival, raw-coordinate recomputability, idempotent re-runs, flag-off legacy behavior, migration up/down).

body:
## Summary

Two foundational, additive changes that improve the core module independently of any UI:

1. **A source-agnostic `StatementSource` ingestion port.** Today transactions enter only via CSV.
   This introduces a small port that yields normalized `ImportedTransaction` batches regardless of
   origin, so the downstream pipeline (duplicate detection, categorization, reconciliation) no longer
   needs to know where transactions came from. A future feed (e.g. an Open Banking connector) becomes
   another implementation of the same interface with no pipeline changes.

2. **An architecture boundary guard** that keeps the domain headless and reusable.

Both are behaviour-preserving: no existing flow changes.

## What changed

### `StatementSource` port (core `bankimport`)
- `StatementSource` — the port: `sourceType()` + `fetch()`.
- `StatementBatch` — the result: the normalized transactions plus provenance (source type, reference,
  detected format).
- `StatementSourceException` — checked failure for unreadable/unparseable sources.
- `CsvStatementSource` — the first implementation, wrapping the existing auto-detecting bank CSV
  pipeline (`BankFormatDetector` + per-bank `BankCsvParser`). The normalized model and the duplicate
  detector already operate on `ImportedTransaction`, so the downstream is already source-agnostic.

### Architecture boundary guard
- `CoreBoundaryTest` (ArchUnit) fails if `core`/`common` classes depend on the JavaFX toolkit, on raw
  JDBC (`java.sql`/`javax.sql`), or on the `ui` module — enforcing that dependencies point inward and
  the domain can run without a UI. Passes on the current clean baseline.
- Adds `archunit-junit5` as a test dependency of `core`.

## Testing
- Full `core` module test suite passes (1825 tests, 0 failures).
- New tests: the CSV source wrapper (detect → parse → batch, no-match and parse-failure mapping); a
  contract test proving an in-memory (non-CSV) source feeds the same processing identically; the three
  boundary rules.

The seat-owner-as-admin prerequisite for PR-4. **Portal already sends the role** (`role: member.role`, `MemberRole = OWNER | ADMIN | MEMBER`, uppercase — `wbit-portal token/route.ts:144`), but PR-3's `require_org_admin` compared against **lowercase** `{executive, owner, admin}`. So an actual org **OWNER** (`"OWNER" != "owner"`) was **not** recognized as admin — and once PR-4 removes the dev flag, real owners would be 403'd from every admin action.

**PR-3's tests masked it** by seeding lowercase `"owner"` — the same "green tests / broken prod" trap as the OWUI-token discovery. Caught by reading Portal's actual claim.

- **`deps.py` `_role_is_admin(role)`** — case-insensitive (`role.lower() in ORG_ADMIN_ROLES`), used on both the legacy Portal path (`portal_auth.role`) and the OWUI path (caller `AgencyOSMember.role`). Both `OWNER` and `ADMIN` → org-admin.
- **`portal-exchange`** — normalize the Portal role to **lowercase** before storing on `AgencyOSMember` (canonical storage).
- **Tests** — use the **real uppercase `OWNER`** on the Portal-JWT path + one OWUI seed (legacy uppercase row), so the suite reflects prod, not stand-ins.

## Result
Full suite **168 passed**. An org owner is now provisioned as a **recognized admin** at exchange. **This unblocks PR-4** (drop the flag → full enforcement).

Sixth hardening batch — the secrets-leak / log-redaction cluster.

- **M01 — channel secrets echoed to the UI.** `GET /api/channels` and `/api/channels/{id}` now mask the Slack/Teams/Discord webhook URLs and PagerDuty routing key (a `****`+last-4 hint), so credentials can't be exfiltrated via the channels API.

`sanitiseJdbcUrl` is now `static` so the CLI/banner call it without injection wiring.

`Config.Validate()` accepted a Job whose `name` starts with `-` (e.g. `-nightly`), but the generated unit invokes `acron run -nightly` (systemd `ExecStart`, launchd `ProgramArguments`), and cobra/pflag parses the leading-dash argument as a flag rather than the job name. So the job passed validation yet could never fire from the scheduler or by hand (`acron run`/`trigger`/`show`/`logs`/`history`). This tightens the name regex to `^[a-z0-9_][a-z0-9_-]*$` (leading `-` rejected; leading `_`, digits, and internal `-` still valid) and syncs the `config --help` schema comment. No currently-working config is affected, since a leading-dash job is already unusable end-to-end.

author: jomcgi
body:
Closes the findings-dependency gap in the scan-perf comparison.

## Problem
The perf harvest discovers a managed scan only by sweeping findings for its `first_seen_scan_id`. A managed scan with **no findings** (the common case) - or a re-scan surfacing nothing new - is therefore invisible, and its runtime can't be retrieved. There is no list-scans API to fall back on.

## Fix
Semgrep's native `semgrep_scan` webhook fires on **every scan completion, including no-findings scans**, and the payload carries the scan id. This adds a `/webhooks/semgrep` endpoint that captures each managed scan's runtime in near-real-time, findings-independent. The hourly harvest stays as the **backstop for missed deliveries**.

- Fail-closed HMAC verification of `X-Semgrep-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 hex) with `SEMGREP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; accepts a match against either the raw body or Semgrep's canonical compact re-serialization.
- Reuses the harvest's `fetch_scan` + `scan_to_row` + `upsert_scan_perf`; our own scans (env UNSPECIFIED) are skipped (report.py owns those).
- Mirrors the GitHub webhook infra: dedicated no-SecurityPolicy HTTPRoute, secret from the semgrep 1Password item as optional env.

## Manual steps after merge
1. Add `SEMGREP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to the semgrep 1Password vault item.
2. Semgrep -> Settings -> Integrations -> Add -> Webhook: URL `https://private.jomcgi.dev/webhooks/semgrep`, signing secret = same value.
3. Cloudflare Access bypass for the `/webhooks/semgrep` path (already configured).

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1625. `S3VirtualHostFilter` hardcoded the wildcard-DNS suffixes (`localhost.floci.io`, `localhost.localstack.cloud`) in two places: the bare service-host check (`isS3ServiceEndpointHost`) and the virtual-hosted bucket fallback (`isAwsS3Domain`). Both now derive their suffix set from the embedded DNS source of truth (`EmbeddedDnsServer.BUILTIN_SUFFIXES`) plus any configured `floci.dns.extra-suffixes`, so a custom DNS suffix is recognised the same way the builtins are.

On #1625 you flagged deriving the service-host list from config as a follow-up ("fine now but worth deriving from config in a follow up"). This does that, and applies the same treatment to the virtual-host bucket path so `extra-suffixes` route buckets consistently, not just resolve in DNS.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (`fix:`)

## What changed

- `buildServiceHostSuffixes()` computes `{localhost}` + `BUILTIN_SUFFIXES` + `extra-suffixes` once per instance; `isS3ServiceEndpointHost()` checks membership instead of string literals.
- `matchesConfiguredSuffixHost()` routes the virtual-hosted forms `bucket.<suffix>`, `bucket.s3.<suffix>` and `bucket.s3.<region>.<suffix>` for every configured suffix, replacing the hardcoded localstack/floci branches in `isAwsS3Domain`.
- `EmbeddedDnsServer.BUILTIN_SUFFIXES` widened to `public` so the filter reuses the canonical list instead of introducing a third copy.

## AWS Compatibility

No wire-format or SDK-visible change. One narrowing: the virtual-host match now requires the full builtin suffix (`.localhost.localstack.cloud`) rather than the bare parent domain (`.localstack.cloud`), so a non-LocalStack host like `bucket.s3.foo.localstack.cloud` no longer routes. This matches LocalStack's actual wildcard DNS (`*.localhost.localstack.cloud`); no existing test covered the broad form. Happy to keep the parent-domain match if you'd prefer it.

## Test plan

- [x] `S3VirtualHostFilterTest` (55 cases (added service-host classification from the derived set + virtual-host routing for a configured extra suffix, with negative cases)
- [x] `S3VirtualHostIntegrationTest`) 19, green
